persona.background: Grew up in Albuquerque's South Valley and earned a B.S. in Civil Engineering from the University of New Mexico in 2013, then an M.S. in Transportation Engineering from Arizona State University in 2015. Started as a junior traffic engineer at Desert Ridge Consulting in Phoenix, and in 2019 moved to Denver to join Front Range Mobility Group, where she is now a senior project engineer designing signal timing and bike-lane retrofits.
persona.personality: Dry-humored, conscientious and a little perfectionist; she over-prepares, hates being late, and deflects stress with jokes. Warm with close friends but slow to ask for help. Likes data, spreadsheets and clear plans, and gets restless when things are ambiguous.

events.title: Denver Half Marathon

preferences: Prefers answers in concise bullet points with the recommendation first, then reasoning.
Likes tables when comparing more than two options.
Wants numbers with units and dates, not vague estimates.
Drinks black coffee in the morning and stops caffeine by 2 p.m.
Eats mostly vegetarian on weekdays but loves her mother's green chile stew.
Uses Notion for planning and Google Calendar for scheduling.
Works in Excel and Python (pandas) for traffic data analysis.
Wakes at 5:45 a.m. and walks the dog at 6:30 a.m.
Does her deep work in the morning and avoids meetings before 10 a.m. when possible.
Climbs at the gym on Tuesday and Thursday evenings.
Dislikes small talk on calls and prefers email over phone for work matters.
Dislikes excessive exclamation points and overly cheerful tone from assistants.
Prefers metric-free US units (miles, Fahrenheit, dollars).
Likes podcasts about urban planning and true crime on commutes.
Budgets with a monthly zero-based spreadsheet and hates unplanned subscription charges.
sensitive_topics: Breakup with Theo Lindqvist in December 2024, after he accepted a Seattle job; she still feels guilt and grief and avoids discussing him casually.
Father Daniel's heart bypass surgery on February 11, 2025, with a complicated recovery in March 2025 including an infection.
Mother Rosa's worsening diabetes and a hospitalization in September 2025 for a foot ulcer, raising worries about care costs.
Money stress: in April 2025 she co-signed part of her parents' medical bills (about $9,400) and drew down her emergency fund, while rent rose to $1,950 in July 2025.
Health scare: in May 2025 she had episodes of heart palpitations and wore a 14-day cardiac monitor; results in June 2025 showed benign arrhythmia but she remains anxious.
Work stress: a project at Front Range Mobility lost funding in January 2026, leading to layoff rumors and her fear of losing her job.
